findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done. The initial lock creation is atomic, but after an ended run leaves a lock, two new runs can both read that stale owner and unlink the lock before either creates its replacement. The comment acknowledges this race. Both runs can then close and merge the same items, breaking the one-run-per-repo guarantee.
findings.title: Not done: stale lock takeover permits two land runs

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Not done. Every `hotspot` is sent straight to Needs you without `close.check_stop` (`src/forge/close.py:464-484`). An unanswered review-loop stop older than 30 minutes therefore never gets the configured default on a later `forge land --all`. A worker-stuck `hotspot` with `stop.question` also gets a review-loop question and `narrow|split|accept` step instead of close's actual `switch|same|narrow|split` refusal. The run gives the wrong next action in both named stop paths.
findings.title: Not done: stopped changes retain close's decision and default rules

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 1
Raise: Test. The GitHub stub logs arguments without the required call times (`tests/test_queue_land_all.py:33-35`), and the test checks parent `Starting` lines rather than when each child actually enters close. It also checks only a live CI wait: it never reruns after killing that close to prove the item is selectable again, and never checks that an already merged pull request is named as left out. Those item-1 behaviors could break while this test passes.
findings.title: Not done: test_1 proves the selection and start-order details
